description: This pie chart illustrates the distribution of question types across difficulty levels – easy, medium, and hard – as related to knowledge crossword geometric reasoning with large language models. The chart is composed of three separate pie charts, one for each difficulty level. The “easy” chart has four slices: a large teal slice representing 55.4%, a smaller orange slice at 38.3%, a light orange slice at 4.7%, and a small red slice at 1.6%. The “medium” chart also has four slices: a teal slice representing 58.8%, an orange slice at 35.4%, a light orange slice at 4.8%, and a red slice at 1.0%. The “hard” chart contains five slices: a teal slice representing 37.3%, an orange slice at 37.9%, a light orange slice at 18.1%, a red slice at 6.7%, and a very small pink slice labeled “N+K+” representing 0.0%. Each chart includes percentage labels displayed inside the slices, and a legend is provided below the charts identifying the categories represented by each color. The slices within each chart appear to be ordered from largest to smallest proportion.
